data.epp:
apiVersion: llm-d.ai/v1alpha1
kind: EndpointPickerConfig
featureGates: [flowControl]
plugins:
  - type: maas-weighted-fairness
    name: maas-fairness
    parameters:
      # x-maas-subscription, NOT x-maas-subscription-id.
      #
      # This was wrong for most of the POC and the failure is silent: with
      # the id suffix the header simply never matches, every request falls
      # to defaultGroup, and unmatched_subscriptions_total stays at ZERO --
      # because nothing was mis-matched, the header was absent. The only
      # symptom is all traffic quietly sharing the `unclassified` weight.
      #
      # Verified against the AuthPolicy MaaS generates per model
      # (maas-auth-<model> in the model namespace), whose success response
      # injects exactly:
      #     X-MaaS-Subscription: auth.metadata.apiKeyValidation.subscription
      # i.e. the MaaSSubscription NAME from the validated sk-oai API key.
      # It also blanks Authorization before forwarding upstream.
      #
      # CONSEQUENCE FOR `groups` BELOW: the match values must be
      # MaaSSubscription names, not invented tenant strings. Confirm with
      #     oc get maassubscriptions -A
      # before trusting any weight in this file.
      identityHeader: x-maas-subscription
      groups:
        # UNI-187 variant: table=6 weights=dominant. Generated by deploy/poc/epp-groups/render.py -- do not hand-edit.
        - { name: app1, weight: 90, match: { exact: [app1-production] } }
        - { name: app2, weight: 2, match: { exact: [app2-batch] } }
        - { name: app3, weight: 2, match: { exact: [app3] } }
        - { name: app4, weight: 2, match: { exact: [app4] } }
        - { name: app5, weight: 2, match: { exact: [app5] } }
        - { name: app6, weight: 2, match: { exact: [app6] } }
      defaultGroup: { name: unclassified, weight: 5 }

      enforce: false
      stateLogIntervalSeconds: 5

      halfLifeSeconds: 60
      observedHalfLivesSeconds: [20, 120]

      costModel: tokens
      inputTokenWeight: 1.0
      outputTokenWeight: 2.0       # PLACEHOLDER until calibrated
      cachedInputTokenWeight: 1.0

      # Left at the production default, but see docs/poc-results.md: in this
      # POC, turning the clamp ON measurably moved the split AWAY from the
      # configured weights (end-users 62.8% -> 45.1%), and it did so while
      # firing only 19 times in 862 dispatches. The highest-weight group is
      # hit hardest, because it is served fastest, so its queue is the one
      # that momentarily drains -- and the clamp writes A = floor * w, so
      # the largest weight loses the most credit per clamp.
      #
      # RESOLVED by UNI-212: the empty -> non-empty edge WAS exactly that
      # poor proxy -- it was keyed to the shared Pick-call sequence, which
      # advances on a ~1ms ticker and on every other group's enqueue, so a
      # momentary drain from efficient service (milliseconds) was
      # indistinguishable from a genuine return from idle (tens of
      # seconds). newcomerClampIdleSeconds below adds a wall-clock gate so
      # only the latter clamps. See docs/design.md "UNI-212: the backlog
      # edge was Pick-cadence-blind".
      newcomerClamp: true
      newcomerClampIdleSeconds: 2
      provisionalCharge: true
      defaultEstimatedOutputTokens: 512
      estimatedBytesPerToken: 4
      agingTokensPerSecond: 0

      # x-request-id, x-maas-fairness-group, x-maas-fairness-queue-ms on the
      # response -- see docs/design.md "Per-request attribution" (UNI-53).
      # Defaults to true; set false to suppress if this is considered
      # internal detail leakage.
      emitAttributionHeaders: true

      # V(4) per-request tier -- see docs/design.md "V(4) is off Pick's hot
      # path" (UNI-47). Off by default; also requires -v=4 on the EPP
      # process. Neither this file nor -v reload without a redeploy.
      # Enabling needs BOTH this and a second edit to deploy/poc/02-epp.yaml,
      # or emission stays silently off -- see docs/runbook.md "Turn on the
      # V(4) per-request tier" for the exact steps and how to undo them.
      # requestTierV4SampleEvery: 100
      # requestTierV4TimeBoxSeconds: 900

  - type: single-profile-handler
  - type: queue-scorer
  - type: kv-cache-utilization-scorer
  - type: prefix-cache-scorer
  - type: max-score-picker

  # UNI-211: the framework's own default saturation detector
  # (utilization-detector, queueDepthThreshold=5) is calibrated for a
  # single endpoint running near-interactive load, not for this backend.
  # The two real vLLM replicas are started with --max-num-seqs 8 (see
  # `oc get deployment maas-vllm-gpu-kserve -o jsonpath='{.spec.template
  # .spec.containers[0].args}'`), and under full-contention's deliberate
  # 12x over-offer their own internal waiting queue (vLLM's
  # num_requests_waiting, surfaced here as llm_d_epp_per_endpoint_
  # queue_size) settles at a steady-state depth of ~85-90 per endpoint
  # even when the backend is fully and continuously utilised (confirmed
  # from the stock-EPP UNI-168 comparison run, which has no admission
  # gate at all: average_running_requests pegged at 7.5-8 throughout,
  # average_queue_size steady around 86-89). A threshold of 5 reads that
  # healthy backlog as 15-18x over saturated and makes dispatchCycle's
  # HoL block (saturation >= usageLimit) fire on almost every cycle --
  # see docs/poc-results.md "UNI-211" for the live evidence this was
  # built from. 150 sat comfortably above the observed steady state but
  # UNI-216 then found it so high that the EPP's own queue almost never
  # backs up at all -- the fairness plugin can only reorder requests the
  # EPP is still holding, so at 150 the split just follows whichever
  # group offered the most workers, not the configured weights.
  #
  # UNI-215 swept {8,16,32,64,150} against that exact failure mode and
  # found 32 is the best point: full-contention (the series' normal
  # 1:1:4 contention case) and F3's balanced 33/33/33 weight set both
  # flip from FAIL to PASS, 40/20/40 improves sharply (-21.6 -> -12.5
  # points, just short of passing), throughput across every run stays
  # within ~5% of the no-admission-control baseline -- but UNI-161's
  # app1-flood (256:32:64, an 8x/4x worker over-offer) and F3's 98/1/1
  # (deliberately stresses the small-weight floor) still FAIL by a wide
  # margin at every threshold from 8 to 150; admission-side holding has
  # a real but bounded ability to correct for extreme worker-count
  # imbalance. See docs/poc-results.md "UNI-215" for the full sweep and
  # confirmation data. Not a universal number and must be re-derived
  # (same method: compare against a no-admission-control baseline) for
  # any other backend or --max-num-seqs value -- see docs/design.md.
  #
  # CAUTION for whoever picks this up next: lowering the default from
  # 150 to 32 means the ~21 of 29 scenarios UNI-216 found UNCONTENDED
  # at 150 (and so never actually exercised the fairness policy) will
  # likely show real contention again at 32 -- UNI-215 did not re-run
  # them. Treat that as an open re-validation, not a settled PASS.
  - type: utilization-detector
    name: maas-saturation
    parameters:
      queueDepthThreshold: 32
      headroom: 0.3

flowControl:
  # 300s here, against 60s in deploy/epp-config.yaml, and this is the one
  # POC deviation that is NOT a simplification.
  #
  # The load generator deliberately over-offers ~12x the pool's capacity so
  # the queues are deep enough for the weights to be expressible. The flip
  # side is that the throttled group waits a long time by design: at a 10%
  # share with 32 closed-loop workers, app2's queue wait approaches a
  # minute. With TTL at 60s those requests would be EVICTED rather than
  # served late -- and then the shed rate, not the fairness policy, is what
  # allocates the pool. The measurement would show app2 "receiving" its
  # share while most of its traffic was quietly dropped.
  #
  # Production keeps TTL within ~2x of halfLifeSeconds precisely so that
  # shedding stays a backstop. Do not copy 300s into a real deployment; it
  # is compensating for a synthetic over-offer that real traffic will not
  # reproduce. Watch llm_d_epp_flow_control_requests_evicted_total: if it
  # is non-zero in a run, that run measured shedding, not fairness.
  defaultRequestTTL: 300s
  saturationDetector:
    pluginRef: maas-saturation
  defaultPriorityBand:
    fairnessPolicyRef: maas-fairness
    orderingPolicyRef: fcfs-ordering-policy
  priorityBands:
    - priority: 0
      fairnessPolicyRef: maas-fairness
      maxRequests: "5000"

# UNI-214: queue-scorer and prefix-cache-scorer carry EQUAL weight (was
# 2.0 / 3.0). queue-scorer is min-max normalized over the candidates
# (shorter queue 1.0, longer 0.0, equal queues 1.0 each), and
# prefix-cache-scorer is matchBlocks/totalBlocks. At 2.0 / 3.0, a replica
# holding a ~99% prefix match kept a constant +1.0 lead however deep its
# queue grew, so the other replica got zero traffic for whole runs
# (UNI-211 Mechanism B). With equal weights, the cold replica wins as soon
# as the warm one's queue is longer, warms its own cache, and from then on
# the queue decides; prefix affinity still decides between equal queues.
# Board-chosen fix (the same one that cleared this lock-in in the
# air-gapped field environment), validated live in docs/poc-results.md
# "UNI-214". kv-cache-utilization-scorer is left at 2.0: KV utilization
# reads 0 on both pods here, so it scores them identically.
schedulingProfiles:
  - name: default
    plugins:
      - { pluginRef: queue-scorer, weight: 3.0 }
      - { pluginRef: kv-cache-utilization-scorer, weight: 2.0 }
      - { pluginRef: prefix-cache-scorer, weight: 3.0 }
      - { pluginRef: max-score-picker }
